newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avg lending rate rises 40 bps to 10.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avg lending rate rises 40 bps to 10.0 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose another 40 basis points to 10.0 percent on Thursday, lifted by a higher volume of term loans.
Trade totalled 47.6 million kuna, against 120 million on offer, and most were fresh loans.
The interbank call money remained stable at 8.0 percent, accounting for just under 20 million kuna.
Term rates ranged between 11 percent for two-week and 16 percent for two-month funds.
Banks extended previous one-month deals at 13 percent.
Insurers rolled over old one-week loans at nine percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday firmer at 6.2285 against the dollar and at 3.5673 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
